sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE LONGWAVE PATTERN WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY AMPLIFIED DURING THE PERIOD WHILE SPLIT UPPER FLOW PERSISTS OVER THE EASTERN THIRD OF THE CONUS. A PERSISTENT UPPER LOW WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD OVER THE ARKLATEX/LOWER MS RIVER VALLEY. AN UPPER RIDGE WILL BUILD OVER THE CENTRAL PLAINS/UPPER MIDWEST AHEAD OF A NORTHEASTWARD-ADVANCING SHORTWAVE TROUGH/UPPER-JET STREAM OVER THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST/NORTHERN ROCKIES.

sections.title: MT/NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF THE NORTHEASTWARD-EJECTING SHORTWAVE TROUGH/JET STREAK...STEADY HEIGHT FALLS AND STRENGTHENING SOUTHWESTERLY WINDS ALOFT WILL OCCUR OVER THE REGION THROUGH TONIGHT. AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT CANNOT BE RULED OUT THIS MORNING IN AREAS SUCH AS FAR EASTERN MT/WESTERN ND...BUT A MORE CONSEQUENTIAL SEVERE RISK IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. A SURFACE LOW WILL STEADILY DEEPEN/DEVELOP NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS CENTRAL/NORTHEAST MT THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WHILE BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CONTENT GRADUALLY INCREASES ACROSS NORTHERN/EASTERN MT AND THE NEARBY DAKOTAS NEAR A NORTHWEST-SOUTHEAST ANGLING WARM FRONT. PRIMARILY 50S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS...AND POSSIBLY NEAR 60 F ACROSS NORTHEAST MT BY EVENING...WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AMPLE INSTABILITY WITH 2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE POSSIBLE WITHIN THE MAIN MOISTURE AXIS EAST-NORTHEAST OF THE SURFACE LOW/NEAR THE WARM FRONT. OWING TO INCREASING FORCING FOR ASCENT/WEAKENING INHIBITION...INITIALLY HIGH-BASED STORMS/SUPERCELLS SHOULD INITIALLY DEVELOP ACROSS CENTRAL MT THIS AFTERNOON IN THE PRESENCE OF 40+ KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR...AND SUBSEQUENTLY SPREAD INTO/DEVELOP ACROSS NORTHERN/EASTERN MT BY EARLY EVENING. LARGE HAIL/DAMAGIN

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: AS THE UPPER LOW CONTINUES A SLOW SOUTHEASTWARD MOVEMENT TODAY OVER THE ARKLATEX/LOWER MS RIVER VALLEY...A BELT OF MODESTLY STRONG MID/LOW-LEVEL WINDS WILL OVERSPREAD A MOIST/POTENTIALLY UNSTABLE BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES. WHILE EARLY-DAY CLOUD COVER AND ONGOING PRECIPITATION PROVIDES SOME UNCERTAINTY...POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING AND AROUND 70 F SURFACE DEWPOINTS SHOULD ALLOW FOR AT LEAST MODEST DESTABILIZATION WITH STORMS INTENSIFYING THIS AFTERNOON. PENDING ADEQUATE DESTABILIZATION...DAMAGING WIND/SOME TORNADO RISK MAY EXIST...PARTICULARLY ACROSS SOUTHERN LA IN AREAS NEAR/SOUTH OF A WEAK SURFACE LOW/WARM FRONT.

sections.title: WY/UT
sections.text: AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT...ISOLATED STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS MAY DEVELOP AS FAR SOUTH AS PARTS OF UT/WEST-CENTRAL WY THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING NEAR A SURFACE TROUGH. WITH RELATIVELY STRONG WINDS ON THE IMMEDIATE ANTICYCLONIC SIDE OF THE NORTHERN INTERMOUNTAIN UPPER JET...A STRONG BELT OF MID/HIGH-LEVEL SOUTHWESTERLY WINDS AND DIURNALLY STEEP LAPSE RATES MAY ALLOW FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINED/QUASI-ORGANIZED CLUSTERS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND POSSIBLY SOME HAIL.

sections.title: DEEP SOUTH TX
sections.text: WHILE THE LIKELIHOOD OF DEEP CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IS NOT CERTAIN...ISOLATED TSTMS COULD DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON IN VICINITY OF A SOUTHWARD-SAGGING WEAK FRONT/SURFACE TROUGH. SHOULD THIS OCCUR...SEVERE TSTMS/SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL WOULD BE POSSIBLE. THIS WOULD BE IN THE PRESENCE OF AMPLE MOISTURE AND INSTABILITY /2000+ J PER KG MLCAPE/ COINCIDENT WITH A MODERATELY STRONG BELT OF NORTHWESTERLY FLOW ALOFT /30-40 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR/.

sections.title: MIDWEST/OH RIVER VALLEY/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER HEATS...TSTMS SHOULD DIURNALLY INCREASE/MATURE IN AREAS ALONG AND SOUTH OF A SLOW SOUTHWARD-MOVING FRONTAL BOUNDARY. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE RATHER LIMITED GIVEN WEAK WESTERLIES /15 KT OR LESS/...BUT ADEQUATELY STEEP LAPSE RATES/CAPE MAY ALLOW FOR PULSE-TYPE STORMS/SOME MULTICELLS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS MARGINAL HAIL.

sections.text: CONUS UPPER-AIR PATTERN THROUGH PERIOD WILL BE DOMINATED BY TWO CYCLONES-- 1. LONG-LIVED...SLOWLY FILLING VORTEX INITIALLY CENTERED OVER ARKLATEX REGION...AND FCST TO DRIFT SEWD TOWARD CENTRAL LA. 2. MERIDIONALLY ELONGATED GYRE NOW MOVING ASHORE WA/ORE COASTS. ATTACHED...POSITIVELY TILTED 500-MB TROUGH WILL EXTEND SWWD ACROSS NERN ORE TO NRN CA BY END OF PERIOD. AT SFC...11Z ANALYSIS SHOWED WAVY FRONTAL ZONE WITH SEVERAL ATTACHED/WEAK LOWS...GENERALLY EXTENDING FROM NJ TO LE AND WWD ACROSS NRN IL...NWWD OVER NRN IA AND EXTREME ERN SD...THROUGH WEAK CYCLONE INVOF FAR...THEN WWD TOWARD DIK...BECOMING DIFFUSED BY OUTFLOW POOL FROM PRIOR/OVERNIGHT MCS. OUTFLOW ARCS SWWD ACROSS S-CENTRAL MT JUST S BIL...THEN NWWD TOWARD LOW OVER S-CENTRAL MT. SLOW-MOVING COLD FRONT WAS ANALYZED FROM THAT LOW SWWD OVER ID...HOWEVER THAT FRONT WILL ACCELERATE EWD ACROSS ID AND WRN MT TODAY WITH APCH OF MID-UPPER-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH. THIS ACTIVITY MAY SPREAD INTO WRN ND THROUGH THE NIGHT...BUT WILL WEAKEN AS NOCTURNAL INHIBITION GROWS. ELSEWHERE...ONGOING STRONG STORMS IN ERN MT MAY POSE A LOCAL SVR RISK

mesoscale_discussions.summary: POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR A FEW...MAINLY BRIEF...TORNADOES THIS MORNING INTO THE AFTERNOON ACROSS SRN AND SERN LA INTO SERN MS. LOCALLY STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE TOO. A TORNADO WATCH WILL BE COORDINATED WITH WFO/S IN THIS AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EARLY-MID MORNING SINGLE-SITE RADAR IMAGERY ACROSS SRN-SERN LA HAS CONTINUED TO INDICATED INTERMITTENT LOW-LEVEL ROTATIONAL COUPLETS IN SRN-SERN LA...MAINLY WITH STORMS THAT DEVELOP AND/OR INTERACT WITH A WSW-ENE ORIENTED SURFACE BOUNDARY IN THIS REGION. THIS BOUNDARY EXTENDED FROM SOUTH-CENTRAL LA /INVOF ST MARY PARISH/ ENEWD TO LAKE PONTCHARTRAIN...AND INTO SERN MS /CLOSE TO A PEARL RIVER TO PERRY COUNTIES CORRIDOR/. EXTENSIVE CLOUD COVER SHOULD LIMIT THE NWD MOVEMENT OF THIS BOUNDARY IN SOUTH-CENTRAL LA...WHILE SOME NWD ADVANCEMENT WILL BE POSSIBLE OVER SERN MS/SWRN AL. A DIFLUENT UPPER-LEVEL FLOW REGIME ACROSS THE NWRN GULF/LOWER MS VALLEY WILL PROMOTE ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT WITHIN A VERY MOIST AND MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. THE PRIMARY THREAT WILL BE FOR MAINLY BRIEF TORNADO DEVELOPMENT WITH STORMS THAT INTERACT AND/OR DEVELOP ALONG THE SURFACE BOUNDARY...GIVEN A VORTICITY-RICH ENVIRONMENT AND RICH MOISTURE /PW OF 1.8-2.0 INCHES/. EFFECTIVE SRH OF 100-200 M2/S2 INVOF THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WILL ENHANCE THE TORNADO POTENTIAL IN A RELATIVELY NARROW CORRIDOR NEAR THE FRONT...WHILE DEEP UNIDIRECTIONAL SLY LOWER-TROPOSPHERIC WINDS SHOULD LIMIT A LONGER-LIVED TORNADO THREAT. IN ADDITION...A WLY LOW-LEVEL JET /50 KT PER LCH WSR-88D VWP/ WITH THE PASSAGE OF A SHORT N-S LINE OF STORMS /NOW LOCATED FROM ACADIA TO ERN CAMERON PARISHES/ SHOULD ENHANCE THE DAMAGING WIND THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS SERN LA INTO SRN MS...AND THROUGH PARTS OF SWRN-WRN AL. GREATEST SEVERE WEATHER RISK IS EXPECTED TO BE CONFINED TO SERN LA INTO SERN MS WITH MAINLY A BRIEF TORNADO AND LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS BEING THE PRIMARY THREATS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TRENDS IN MOSAIC RADAR IMAGERY INTO THE EARLY AFTERNOON INDICATED A FEW BANDS OF TSTMS ADVANCING ENEWD ACROSS WW 195 IN SERN LA AND SRN MS. ADDITIONAL...MORE LOOSELY-DEFINED...BROKEN BANDS OF STORMS CONTINUED TO DEVELOP IN SWRN-WRN AL...WHILE RADAR IMAGERY ALSO SHOWED DISCRETE STORMS FORMING AT TIMES OVER SERN LA AND SERN MS TO THE WRN FL PANHANDLE. TRENDS IN SINGLE-SITE RADAR IMAGERY INDICATED INTERMITTENT...WEAK LOW-LEVEL ROTATING COUPLETS ACROSS SERN LA INTO SERN MS...AND A FEW IN SWRN-WRN AL. VERY RICH MOISTURE /SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE LOWER 70S/ EXISTS ALONG AND SOUTH OF A SLOW NWD MOVING BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM SERN MS INTO SWRN AL. RELATIVELY STRONGER /AROUND 30 KT/ FLOW WITHIN THE SRN AND ERN PERIPHERY OF A WEAKENING CLOSED LOW CENTERED OVER THE ARKLATEX IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN OVER THE EXISTING WATCH AREA. MEANWHILE... EFFECTIVE SRH OF 100-200 M2/S2 PERSISTS INVOF THE WSW-ENE ORIENTED SURFACE BOUNDARY TO SUPPORT A CONTINUED TORNADO THREAT THIS AFTERNOON. WEAKER MID-UPPER LEVEL WINDS INTO WRN AL WILL LIMIT THE SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL/ADDITIONAL WATCH ISSUANCE TO THE E/NE OF WW 195. THE STRONGER WINDS ALOFT ARE EXPECTED TO WEAKEN FURTHER THROUGH THE AFTERNOON... SUCH THAT STORM ORGANIZATION WILL BECOME LESS OF A POTENTIAL THAN IS PRESENT IN THE SHORT TERM. ..PETERS.. 05/28/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL OR WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE BUT A WATCH IS NOT LIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS ARE BEGINNING TO LINE UP ALONG A WEAK BOUNDARY ENHANCED BY DIFFERENTIAL HEATING FROM CNTRL OH SEWD INTO NRN VA. STRONG HEATING WILL PERSIST WHICH WILL FAVOR A CONTINUED INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE. WIND PROFILES ARE WEAK AND THEREFORE AN ORGANIZED SEVERE THREAT IS NOT LIKELY. HOWEVER...STRONG INSTABILITY WILL FAVOR MARGINAL HAIL WITH THE STRONGEST CORES...WITH LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS ALWAYS POSSIBLE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED STRONG-SVR TSTM IS POSSIBLE THROUGH THE MID-LATE AFTERNOON INVOF A SWD MOVING FRONT ACROSS DEEP SOUTH TX. A SOMEWHAT LIMITED POTENTIAL FOR GREATER SVR WEATHER THREAT/COVERAGE PRECLUDES THE NEED FOR A WATCH AT THIS TIME. STRONGER STORMS THAT DEVELOP COULD PRODUCE SOME HAIL AND LOCALLY STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG SURFACE HEATING /TEMPERATURES INTO THE LOWER 90S/ SOUTH OF A BOUNDARY ADVANCING SWD THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS DEEP SOUTH TX HAS REDUCED INHIBITION /PER MODIFICATION OF 12Z BRO SOUNDING/ FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE-BASED STORMS. VERY RICH MOISTURE /SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE LOWER-MID 70S AND PW OF 1.5-1.75 INCHES/ IS CONTRIBUTING TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT /MLCAPE 2000-2500 J PER KG/. THIS COMBINED WITH 30 KT NWLY 500 MB WINDS AND SLY SURFACE WINDS IS RESULTING IN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR 30-40 KT SUPPORTIVE OF STORM ORGANIZATION...INCLUDING A SUPERCELL. THESE FACTORS WOULD TEND TO SUPPORT HAIL AND STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS AS THE PRIMARY THREATS. THE EXPECTED LOW COVERAGE POTENTIAL FOR STRONGER-SEVERE STORMS IS EXPECTED TO PRECLUDE THE NEED FOR A WATCH AT THIS TIME AS THE SURFACE BOUNDARY SHOULD REACH THE TX/MEXICO BORDER BY 22-23Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS FROM HIGH-BASED TSTMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. SOMEWHAT LIMITED COVERAGE OF THE SVR WEATHER THREAT RESULTS IN NO WATCH ISSUANCE AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG SURFACE HEATING ACROSS NRN UT INTO WRN/NRN WY COMBINED WITH DEW POINTS IN THE UPPER 20S-LOWER 30S HAS RESULTED IN LARGE DEW POINT DEPRESSIONS OF 45-55 DEGREES. MIDLEVEL MOISTURE SPREADING NEWD ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA WITH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES /8.5-9.5 C PER KM/ HAS RESULTED IN HIGH-BASED STORMS...GIVEN THE INVERTED-V THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES PER AFOREMENTIONED DRY SUB-CLOUD ENVIRONMENT. THE GOES-R CLOUD TOP COOLING PRODUCT INDICATED COOLING TOPS OVER SWRN TO WEST-CENTRAL WY AND ONGOING CLOUD TOP COOLING IN NERN UT. GIVEN THE FAVORABLE DEEP BOUNDARY LAYER WITH DCAPE 1000-1500 J/KG...STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE...BUT WEAK INSTABILITY SHOULD LIMIT THE OVERALL COVERAGE OF STRONGER-SEVERE STORMS AND THE NEED FOR A SVR TSTM WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM LATER THIS AFTERNOON...WITH LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS AND A TORNADO OR TWO EXPECTED. A WATCH IS LIKELY BY 21Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS A CONTINUED INFLUX OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE NWWD INTO CNTRL MT WHERE STRONG HEATING ALSO PERSISTS. THE PRESENCE OF COOL TEMPERATURES ALOFT AS WELL AS AMPLE DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS RESULTING IN A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND/OR BOWING SEGMENTS WITH DAMAGING WINDS. THE BEST TORNADO THREAT WOULD APPEAR TO BE ACROSS CNTRL AND NRN MT WHERE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR IS STRONGER AND WHERE LCL HEIGHTS WILL REMAIN LOWEST. ANY SUPERCELLS FORMING UPSTREAM AND MOVING INTO THIS ENVIRONMENT COULD PRODUCE A TORNADO...ASSUMING OUTFLOW DOES NOT GET OUT OF HAND.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS MOVING THROUGH SERN MS WILL CONTINUE TO HAVE MAINLY A BRIEF TORNADO THREAT AND POTENTIAL FOR LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS. ALTHOUGH THE MS STORMS SHOULD SPREAD INTO SWRN AL...A DECREASE IN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AND FORCING ATTENDANT TO LARGE SCALE ASCENT WITH EWD EXTENT AWAY FROM THE WEAKENING LOWER MS VALLEY CLOSED LOW SHOULD LIMIT THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED...BUT A NEW WATCH IS NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME TO THE EAST OF WW 195.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MOIST LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENCE EXTENDS NWD INTO SERN MS TO ADJACENT SWRN AL. THIS COMBINED WITH ASCENT ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF A DECAYING MCS MOVING INTO THE ERN PART OF WW 195 SHOULD CONTINUE TO PROMOTE NEW TSTM DEVELOPMENT INTO THE EARLY EVENING...WHERE THE AIR MASS REMAINS MODERATELY UNSTABLE. THIS WOULD INCLUDE STORMS MOVING INTO SWRN AL. TRENDS IN MOB WSR-88D VAD SHOWED STRENGTHENING SLY WINDS IN THE 1-2.5 KM AGL LAYER SINCE 1930Z...ENHANCING 0-1 KM AND 0-3 KM SRH FOR A CONTINUED TORNADO THREAT YET THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS SERN MS. FURTHER WEAKENING AND SUBSEQUENT INFLUENCE WITH THE LOWER MS VALLEY CLOSED SHOULD LIMIT THE EWD EXTENT OF THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT SUCH THAT A NEW WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME INTO SWRN AL. ..PETERS.. 05/28/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL CONTINUES ACROSS CENTRAL AND ERN MT AND ADJACENT NRN WY...WITH THE GREATEST RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS APPARENT ACROSS N CENTRAL MT ATTM. WIND PROBABILITY WITHIN THE SPC 01Z OUTLOOK WILL BE INCREASED TO REFLECT THE EVOLVING SEVERE RISK ACROSS N CENTRAL AND NERN MT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS TWO MAIN CLUSTERS OF STORMS ATTM -- ONE ACROSS E CENTRAL MT AND A SECOND OVER N CENTRAL MT MOVING ENEWD AWAY FROM THE GTF VICINITY ATTM. BOTH CLUSTERS OF STORMS ARE MOVING INTO A FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT...WHERE ESELY LOW-LEVEL FLOW CONTINUES TO ADVECT LOW 60S DEWPOINTS INTO ERN AND NRN MT ATTM. THUS...SEVERE RISK REMAINS APPARENT ACROSS THIS REGION. THE STORMS OVER N CENTRAL MT -- INVOF AN ADVANCING COLD FRONT AND WITHIN THE ZONE OF STRONGEST DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AHEAD OF THE MAIN UPPER TROUGH -- HAVE BECOME PARTICULARLY ORGANIZED...SHOWING TENDENCY FOR BOTH BOWING STRUCTURES AND SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS. ALONG WITH RISK FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL MAY INCREASE FURTHER IN THE NEAR TERM AS SOME POTENTIAL FOR UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A BOWING MCS IS EVIDENT. GREATEST LIKELIHOOD FOR THE MOST SUBSTANTIAL/WIDESPREAD SEVERE WEATHER WILL EXIST OVER THE NEXT 3-4 HOURS...AFTER WHICH THE DIURNALLY STABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER WILL YIELD A GRADUAL DECREASE IN CONVECTIVE INTENSITY/SEVERE RISK. ..GOSS.. 05/29/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE RISK CONTINUES ACROSS THE NERN MT VICINITY...PARTICULARLY OVER THE TIER OF COUNTIES ADJACENT TO THE U.S./CANADIAN BORDER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP CONTINUES TO SHOW TWO MAIN CLUSTERS OF CONVECTION ATTM -- ONE OVER BLAINE CO MT AND THE OTHER MOVING ACROSS THE MCCONE/PRAIRIE/DAWSON CO MT AREA. WHILE ISOLATED SEVERE WEATHER REMAINS POSSIBLE WITH THIS ERN MT STORM CLUSTER...GREATER SEVERE RISK PERSISTS WITH THE MORE ORGANIZED N CENTRAL MT STORMS. STORMS WITHIN THIS CLUSTER REMAIN MUCH MORE ORGANIZED/INTENSE -- EXHIBITING BOTH BOWING AND SUPERCELL STRUCTURES. WHILE SEVERE RISK WILL EVENTUALLY DIMINISH AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES AND AS MORE INTENSE STORMS EVENTUALLY SHIFT INTO SRN SASKATCHEWAN... POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/DAMAGING GUSTS REMAINS LIKELY ACROSS NERN MT AS STORMS MOVE QUICKLY ENEWD OVER THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS. ..GOSS.. 05/29/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
